objects.title: Walk.ofIncrements
objects.statement: ofIncrements (initial : Position) (increment : Nat -> Mark) : Walk Mark Position
objects.summary: Builds a one-branch walk from an initial position and a sequence of increments.
objects.proof: The construction is computational: the unique child slot at generation n reads increment n.

objects.title: Walk.position_lineNode
objects.statement: position n = initial + sum (k < n) (d (increment k))
objects.summary: The formal bridge from an increment sequence to the visible position path.
objects.proof: Induct on the generation. The successor case is the displacement append lemma followed by sum_range_succ.
proofSteps: rewrite the new position as the previous position plus one increment

objects.title: survivingParticlesAt
objects.statement: survivingParticlesAt beta k = { p | p survives beta and generation p = k }
objects.summary: The generation slice of the realized genealogy, independent of the visualization.
objects.proof: The set is a deterministic slice of survivingParticles; different generations are disjoint.

objects.title: M1Corridor
objects.summary: A finite-step upper and lower boundary defining a strict corridor for cadlag paths.
objects.proof: The corridor set requires the path to start at zero and stay strictly between both boundaries.

objects.title: isM1_corridorSet
objects.summary: Every explicit finite-step corridor is an M1 path class.
objects.proof: Package the two boundaries into an M1Corridor and use its defining set.
proofSteps: construct M1Corridor from upper and lower

objects.title: M2Corridor.energy
objects.statement: energy alpha c = integral of widthCost alpha upper lower
objects.summary: The corridor width energy used by the M2 rate-function layer.
objects.proof: The implementation is an extended-real integral; finite step boundaries reduce it to finitely many level cells.
